```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(lme4)
library(lmerTest)
```

# Data

Long-form feature listing data (one row per participant, cue, and feature word). All idiosyncratic responses are kept.

```{r load-data}
fl <- read_csv("../data/08_words.csv")
glimpse(fl)
```

```{r data-summary}
fl %>%
  summarise(
    participants = n_distinct(subject_id),
    cues = n_distinct(cue),
    features = n_distinct(word),
    rows = n()
  )
```

# Predictors

## Concreteness norms

Brysbaert et al. (2014) concreteness ratings (1 = abstract, 5 = concrete), joined to both cues and features.

```{r concreteness}
conc <- read_csv("../data/concreteness_norms.csv")

fl <- fl %>%
  left_join(conc %>% select(cue = word, cue_concrete = concreteness), by = "cue") %>%
  left_join(conc %>% select(word, feature_concrete = concreteness), by = "word")

fl %>%
  summarise(
    cue_coverage = mean(!is.na(cue_concrete)),
    feature_coverage = mean(!is.na(feature_concrete))
  )
```

## Feature frequency

Frequency of a feature within a cue (number of participants who listed it). Collocational frequency (for example from OpenSubtitles) is still TODO.

```{r frequency}
pairs <- fl %>%
  group_by(cue, word, cue_concrete, feature_concrete) %>%
  summarise(feature_frequency = n_distinct(subject_id), .groups = "drop") %>%
  filter(!is.na(cue_concrete), !is.na(feature_concrete))

nrow(pairs)
```

# Cue concreteness vs. feature concreteness

Using features as Y and cues as X, we expect a strong correlation but also a higher intercept (Dunning-Kruger-like pattern?). Cue-level means avoid weighting cues by how many features they have.

```{r correlation}
cue_means <- pairs %>%
  group_by(cue, cue_concrete) %>%
  summarise(mean_feature_concrete = mean(feature_concrete),
            mean_feature_concrete_weighted = weighted.mean(feature_concrete, feature_frequency),
            .groups = "drop")

cor.test(cue_means$cue_concrete, cue_means$mean_feature_concrete)

m_cue <- lm(mean_feature_concrete ~ cue_concrete, data = cue_means)
summary(m_cue)

ggplot(cue_means, aes(cue_concrete, mean_feature_concrete)) +
  geom_point(alpha = .4) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm") +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(x = "Cue concreteness", y = "Mean feature concreteness",
       caption = "Dashed line: feature = cue") +
  theme_minimal()
```

# Mixed model

Semantic distance is not available yet, so this first model uses cue concreteness and feature frequency only. Feature concreteness is a property of the word, so it is constant across cues and people: a random intercept for feature word would absorb all of its variance and make the model degenerate. Only cue is random here.

```{r model}
m1 <- lmer(
  feature_concrete ~ cue_concrete + scale(feature_frequency) + (1 | cue),
  data = pairs
)
summary(m1)
```
